evidence: src/application/services/OrderLookupService.ts: OrderLookupService.getById calls this.orders.findById and throws new NotFoundError('Order', orderId) if nothing is found.

src/application/services/StockAllocationService.ts: StockAllocationService.load calls this.products.findById for each ProductQuantity and throws new NotFoundError('Product', productId); persist calls this.products.save.
Both services use only domain repository interfaces (OrderRepository, ProductRepository) and the shared domain NotFoundError, so they use the same abstractions in the same way.

The graph shows the use cases (CancelOrderUseCase, ShipOrderUseCase, PlaceOrderUseCase, etc.) inject these services through their constructors, which matches the module's role as shared application helpers.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module src/application/services holds two small application-level helper services. Each wraps a domain repository so the order use cases can load aggregates and get a uniform not-found failure. OrderLookupService wraps OrderRepository. StockAllocationService wraps ProductRepository and also persists products after stock moves. Both deal with loading aggregates for use cases and handle a missing aggregate the same way, by throwing the domain NotFoundError. Neither file goes around the module's own abstractions: both depend only on domain repository interfaces and domain types. No rule or invariant is duplicated. The not-found check appears in both files, but it applies to different aggregates (Order and Product) and uses the shared NotFoundError, so the error rule lives in the domain and is not re-implemented here. The two files are separate classes, but they don't split into unrelated concerns. Together they form one cohesive layer of shared loading helpers used by the order use cases.
